sections.title: High probability
sections.content:
Expressing that something is very likely:
• bound to — certain to. She's bound to pass the exam — she's very well prepared.
• inevitable — unavoidable. Delays are inevitable during the construction work.
• undoubtedly — without a doubt. She is undoubtedly the most qualified candidate.
• in all likelihood — very probably. In all likelihood, the project will be completed on time.
• odds are — it's probable. The odds are that prices will continue to rise.

sections.title: Low probability and uncertainty
sections.content:
Expressing doubt or low likelihood:
• unlikely — probably won't happen. It's unlikely that we'll finish before Friday.
• doubtful — seeming unlikely. It's doubtful whether they'll accept the offer.
• remote chance — a very small possibility. There's only a remote chance of success.
• supposedly — according to what is believed. The new system is supposedly much faster.
• conceivable — possible to imagine. It's conceivable that technology will solve the problem.

exercises.question: 'Bound to happen' means it is:
exercises.explanation: Bound to means certain or sure to.

exercises.question: A very small possibility is a ___ chance:
exercises.explanation: A remote chance is a very small possibility.

exercises.question: Something that seems unlikely or uncertain is:
exercises.hint: You're not sure it will happen.

exercises.question: 'In all likelihood' means:
exercises.explanation: In all likelihood means very probably; almost certainly.

exercises.question: 'Supposedly' indicates information that is:
exercises.explanation: Supposedly means according to what is generally assumed or believed.

exercises.question: Something possible to imagine, even if unlikely, is:
exercises.explanation: Conceivable means capable of being imagined or grasped mentally.
